newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Mergers seen snowballing in Manila banking sector.
newsitem.headline: Mergers seen snowballing in Manila banking sector.

text.p: Mergers and acquisitions would be the buzzwords in the Philippine banking industry especially after authorities imposed a hefty increase in the banks' minimum capital base, analysts said.

The Central Bank announced on Thursday it would require universal banks to raise their minimum capital to 4.5 billion pesos ($171.3 million) from the present 2.5 billion pesos ($95.2 million), and for commercial banks to 2.0 billion pesos ($76.1 million) from the present 1.25 billion pesos ($4.76 million).
In the same announcement, the Central Bank said it was cutting reserve requirements to 13 percent from 15.
Existing banks have two years to comply with the new minimum capital level while new banks will have to comply immediately.

The Central Bank's decision on higher capital adequacy norms coincided with an announcement by AsianBank Corp, a unit of A. Soriano Corp and Phinma Group, and PDCP Bank, an affiliate of Metro Pacific Corp, that they were planning a merger.
AsianBank is one of the leaders in investment banking, while PDCP Bank is strong in consumer and retail banking. The merger, if it goes through, will be effected in first quarter 1997.
AsianBank chairman Ramon del Rosario Jr, said in a statement that the merger is necessary for the bank to compete more aggressively with large universal banks.

"There's a likelihood that many small banks will be acquired by big banks ... The merger (plan of AsianBank and PDCP Bank) is a sign of things to come," Audi Pantillano, banking analyst of Angping Securities, told Reuters.
He said many local banks were on the lookout for possible partners in order to compete in a liberalised industry.
Earlier this year, there were two merger and acquisition in the industry.
The Bank of the Philippine Islands merged with CityTrust Banking Corp while PDCP Bank acquired the assets of First Bank of the Philippines.
Other banks which are currently seeking partners are Security Bank, Equitable Banking Corp, and Union Bank of the Philippines, which is a product of a merger itself, industry sources said.
"Size is important in a liberalised environment. Banks need a lot of resources to be able to face competition," Raul Ruiz, vice president for research of Sun Hung Kai Securities, said.
There are 21 universal banks and 30 commercial banks operating in the country. Among them are 14 foreign banks which include some of the biggest in the world.

Johnny Noe Ravalo, economist of the Bankers Association of the Philippines, said mergers and acquisitions would be one of the options banks could choose to be able comply with the new capital adequacy norms.

"For some banks, merger might be the answer. Some banks might look for other partners, while some banks might ask the same partners to produce more money. Each bank has its own strategy," Ravalo said.
